summary: This script creates a relational database schema for managing organizational data, including geographic regions and countries, physical locations, departments, job definitions, employees, and their dependents. Each table links to others through foreign keys with cascade rules, meaning if a parent record is updated or deleted, all related child records are automatically updated or deleted too.

explanations.2: SERIAL is a special type that automatically generates a unique number for each new row, so you don't have to provide one manually.
explanations.7: CHARACTER (2) means exactly 2 characters, fixed-width—this makes sense for country codes like 'US' or 'UK' which are always 2 letters.
explanations.10: ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE means if a region changes its ID or gets deleted, all countries in that region automatically get updated or deleted too, keeping the data consistent.
explanations.33: NUMERIC (8, 2) means a number with up to 8 total digits where exactly 2 are after the decimal point—perfect for dollar amounts like 50000.00.
explanations.46: manager_id points back to the employees table itself, letting you represent a hierarchy where each employee can have a manager who is also an employee.
explanations.50: This self-referential foreign key with CASCADE rules means if you delete an employee who is someone's manager, that relationship is automatically cleaned up.
